stories.topic: GLOBAL MARKETS / AI / EQUITIES / UST / CREDIT / FUND FLOWS
stories.headline: Global equity funds lose US$22.73bn while government-bond funds attract inflows
stories.body: Reuters reported LSEG Lipper data showing net global equity-fund withdrawals of US$22.73 billion in the week ended 25 November 2026, the largest weekly outflow in 14 months. US and Asian equity funds lost US$30.57 billion and US$2.75 billion respectively, while European equity funds gained US$7.29 billion. Global bond funds lost US$3.51 billion overall, despite US$7.14 billion entering government-bond funds; high-yield funds lost US$1.54 billion. These are weekly fund flows, not prices, investment returns or current-day trading. Selected regional and bond categories are not necessarily additive.
stories.analysis: Investors can reduce equity and lower-quality credit exposure while selectively buying government debt. Fund inflows alone do not guarantee a positive bond-price return.
stories.watch_next: Subsequent weekly flows, credit spreads and evidence of AI-related cash generation.

stories.topic: SINGAPORE / BOC AVIATION / CORPORATE CREDIT / AIRLINES
stories.headline: Norse Atlantic disputes notices terminating leases across its 12-aircraft fleet
stories.body: Reuters reported Norse Atlantic receiving termination notices for leases covering all 12 aircraft in its fleet. The airline contested their validity and continued seeking urgent short-term funding. The lessors included AerCap and Singapore-based BOC Aviation. Reuters recorded Norse shares down 45% at 08:37 GMT on 27 November, or 16:37 SGT, with a 99.6% year-to-date decline. Those are dated share observations, not current quotes. At the source report’s 20:29:27 SGT cutoff, this reviewed development did not establish a formal bankruptcy filing or a quantified loss for either lessor; later developments are outside this edition.
stories.analysis: Lease termination notices add operational uncertainty to financing pressure. Airline liquidity, contractual disputes and any actual lessor losses require separate assessment.
stories.watch_next: Funding announcements, resolution of lease disputes and any subsequent formal insolvency filing.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 covered the 26 November flight suspension and a bankruptcy warning conditional on financing failure. This v2 adds the disputed lease termination notices and preserves that earlier context.

stories.headline: Indonesia police announce three arrests in alleged Dian Swastatika share manipulation
stories.body: Reuters reported Indonesian police announcing three arrests over alleged manipulation of Dian Swastatika Sentosa trading volumes to meet MSCI index-inclusion criteria. Police alleged profits of IDR10 trillion from overseas-account transactions. These are police allegations, not convictions or independently established realised profits. The company did not immediately respond to Reuters. No isolated share-price reaction or newly completed MSCI market reclassification was verified in this edition.
stories.analysis: Criminal enforcement adds a substantive development to the retained ownership-transparency and index-eligibility event. Allegations and any eventual index decision remain distinct.
stories.watch_next: Court proceedings, company responses, ownership disclosures and MSCI’s assessment.
stories.earlier: Retained v1 described Indonesia’s MSCI-related market risks; v2 added MSCI’s consultation clarification; v3 added exchange penalties for five issuers. The producer’s sanctions alias v1 maps to retained v3. Its new police-enforcement alias v2 therefore becomes canonical v4, preserving all three predecessors rather than duplicating or restarting the same event.

stories.topic: INDIA / RBI / USD / IG CREDIT / BONDS
stories.headline: IIFCL and UCO Bank consider debut US-dollar bond offerings before RBI hedge window closes
stories.body: Bankers told Reuters that India Infrastructure Finance Company (IIFCL) could seek about US$500 million through five-year bonds, while UCO Bank could issue US$250–300 million with a three- or five-year maturity. They were considering issuance before the Reserve Bank of India’s subsidised hedging window closes on 31 December 2026. Reuters reported IIFCL’s S&P Global Ratings assessment at BBB, and UCO debt rated BBB by S&P Global Ratings and BBB− by Fitch. The amounts, maturities and timing remain prospective; no final coupon, issue spread, issuance yield or completed fundraising was established.
stories.analysis: Benchmark Treasury yields, issuer credit spreads and currency hedging costs jointly determine financing economics. A proposed issue is separate from funds received or an actual borrowing cost.
stories.watch_next: Offering documents, final pricing and ratings, investor demand and the hedge-window deadline.

stories.headline: Turkey’s fund crisis restricts capital-market issuance and leaves IPO applicants waiting
stories.body: Reuters described financing pressure following Turkey’s September investment-fund collapse. Corporate bond issue counts fell from 119 in August 2026 to 102 in September and 74 in October. Some 119 companies were awaiting IPO approval, with no new IPO approvals since the crisis. These are counts of issues and pending applicants, not borrowing volumes, prices or a count of corporate defaults. The article is an older recovered development, originally dated 26 November; its exact original publication minute was not independently verified for this preview.
stories.analysis: Liquidity and confidence problems can constrain refinancing even when no economy-wide default is established. The issue counts do not by themselves quantify losses or future credit performance.
stories.watch_next: Regulatory measures, investor repayments and the recovery of primary-market issuance.
